taste.name: Um provedor decide o material; os componentes obedecem
taste.trigger: When the designers faced 38 glass components that must all respect the same theme and accessibility settings on every user's device
taste.decision: Chose one GlassProvider that holds the preferences and writes them as data-lg-* attributes on the html element over per-component props or CSS switches
taste.reason: Because a user who turns on Reduce Transparency expects every glass surface to change at once; one source of truth makes that a single write
evidence: API text: Holds the preferences and writes them to data-lg-* attributes on the html element
useOptionalPreferences returns defaults outside the provider and follows the system reduced-transparency setting
6 preferences: theme, mode, quality, reduceMotion, reduceTransparency, thickness

taste.name: Qualidade detectada pelo aparelho, com a escolha do usuário acima
taste.trigger: When the designers faced a refraction effect that costs real GPU time on phones and low-memory machines
taste.decision: Chose to derive quality automatically (low with reduced transparency or 4 GB of memory or less, medium on touch or reduced motion, high otherwise) and let a saved user choice always win
taste.reason: Because a weak device that stutters makes the material look broken, while a lower tier that stays smooth keeps the look; the override keeps control with the person
evidence: API table: low with reduced transparency or 4 GB of device memory or less, medium on touch or with reduced motion, otherwise high
defaultTheme: A saved choice always wins
reduceTransparency turns off the lens and refraction

taste.name: Espessura como multiplicador limitado, não como estilo
taste.trigger: When the designers faced letting products make the glass thicker or thinner without breaking legibility
taste.decision: Chose one number, thickness, defined as a multiple of regular glass (default 1) clamped to 0.25 to 2, over exposing raw bevel, blur and refraction values
taste.reason: Because a bounded multiplier scales every material parameter together and cannot be pushed to the extremes where text turns unreadable
evidence: API row: Glass thickness as a multiple of regular; applied between 0.25 and 2, type number, default 1

taste.name: Restraint: documentação plana em volta de um único palco de vidro
taste.trigger: When the designers faced a documentation page for a glass library and the pull to make every surrounding panel glass too
taste.decision: Chose a flat page (background #FAF9F7, white menus and tables with a 1px ring, 12 to 14px text) and spent backdrop effects on four nodes, with the lens only in the preview stage, over glass sidebars, tables and code blocks
taste.reason: Because the material is only readable against a plain background; if the documentation chrome were glass too, the preview would stop being the one place where refraction is the subject
evidence: backdrop-filter on 4 nodes in a 5087px page
grid 220px 684px 200px with 56px gap and four equal 56px section gaps
preview stage 684x363px with 28px radius is the only large colour mass
